followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task content.

On **capability**, Willet's benchmarks are higher across the board on the dimensions this task touches — Creative Generation (84.7 vs 78.8), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6, which matters because the request has specific formatting constraints: 120 words, active voice, h4 sub-headings, no tags on paragraphs), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4). These gaps exceed the 2.0-point "tie" threshold, so they're meaningful.

On **content**, the only documented differentiator between the two models is their preference response to distasteful or harm-adjacent material. This tattoo-description task is entirely benign, so that distinguishing factor doesn't apply — there's no reason to reserve the moderation-hardened model here.

With content neutral, the decision reduces to capability, and Willet is the stronger model on every relevant axis. So it was a straightforward pick.
